auditFix.issue: The gloss is too narrow. 몰다 broadly means 'to drive' — its primary modern senses are driving a vehicle (차를 몰다), herding animals, and driving someone into a corner (궁지에 몰다). Restricting it to 'cattle' and 'herd' suggests a rural-only word and misses the everyday vehicle sense that a TOPIK learner is likely to encounter.

The gloss covers only one of two everyday senses. 메다 also means 'to be choked up / blocked / clogged' — the standard collocations 목이 메다 (one's throat is choked up, with emotion or food) and 가슴이 메다 (one's chest is choked) are TOPIK-level vocabulary and appear far more often in narrative dialogue than the 'sling on shoulder' sense. A learner reading 가슴이 메다 in-game with only 'to carry on the shoulder' as the gloss would be misled. Mirrors the auditFix style applied to 몰다 (idx 1) where a narrow gloss was widened.

다 in the sense 'all/entirely/everything' is an adverb (and sometimes noun), not a verb or adjective. Under the file's convention 'verb/adj' is reserved for predicate stems ending in -다; bare 다 'all' belongs in the 'noun/adv' bucket like 늘, 곧, 모두, etc.

The single gloss 'department' is too narrow. 부 (部) primarily means 'part/section/division' and is a counter for copies of a book/newspaper (책 한 부); 부 (副) is the prefix 'vice-/deputy-'; 부 (富) means 'wealth/riches'. 'Department' is one specialised reading (e.g. 인사부) but is not the headword sense.

The 'door' sense is incorrect — that is 문, not 호. 호 (號) means 'number/issue' (잡지 5월호, 101호) and is a counter for housing units; 호 (湖) means 'lake' (백두산 천지호); 호 (號) can also mean a courtesy/pen name. 'Door' looks like a confusion with the Chinese character 戶 (household), which is not a standalone Korean noun for 'door'.

Both senses listed are misleading. 'Sweet (prefix)' is not 단 standalone — it is the attributive form of 달다 (단 호박 = sweet pumpkin), a conjugation, not a lemma. 'Paragraph' is also off; the standalone noun 단 means 'platform/dais; bunch/sheaf (of vegetables); rank/level (martial arts dan); section/tier'. Paragraph in writing is typically 단락 or 문단, not bare 단.

entries.gloss: (time) since (bound noun used in -(으)ㄴ 지 ... 되다)

auditFix.issue: 'ago' is the wrong English equivalent. 지 is a dependent (bound) noun used in the construction -(으)ㄴ 지 X 되다 to express 'X (time) has passed since (the action)'. It marks the elapsed duration since an event, i.e. 'since', not 'ago'. 'ago' in Korean is 전 (e.g., 3년 전 'three years ago'), and 전 is the structural opposite of this 지. Glossing 지 as 'ago' will cause learners to confuse 지 with 전 and produce ungrammatical sentences like *3년 지 instead of 한국에 온 지 3년 됐다 ('it's been 3 years since I came to Korea'). Also 'suffix' is misleading — 지 is a bound noun, not a suffix.

Confirmed: 말다 has two homophonous verbs — 말다₁ 'to roll up' (김밥을 말다, 소매를 말다) and 말다₂ the auxiliary verb in -지 말다 negative imperatives. The auditor's suggestion accurately captures both senses including the auxiliary status.

'To be hateful' implies the subject is the one feeling hatred, which is the opposite of 밉다's meaning. 밉다 is a descriptive verb meaning the subject is the object of dislike — 'to be disliked, to look unpleasant, to be ugly/loathsome'. A more accurate gloss is 'to be despicable, to be hated/disliked' or 'to be ugly (in behaviour or looks)'.

바다 is unambiguously a noun meaning 'sea'. The partOfSpeech tag 'verb/adj' is wrong; it should be 'noun/adv' to match the convention used for the other noun entries in the file. The gloss itself is correct.

Confirmed: 술잔 (술 'alcohol' + 잔 'cup') specifically denotes a vessel for alcohol — wineglass, shot glass, sake cup. wordrow.kr lists it as 'WINEGLASS; WINE CUP; GOBLET'. The generic 'drinking cup' could mislead learners.

Confirmed: 짓 in modern Korean carries strong pejorative connotation (미친 짓, 나쁜 짓, 바보 같은 짓). Wiktionary explicitly notes 'in Modern Korean the word virtually always has a negative connotation.' Neutral 'act, gesture' loses critical semantic information.

entries.gloss: meat (also archaic / in compounds: fish, as in 물고기)

auditFix.issue: Confirmed: in modern Korean, 고기 primarily means 'meat'. The 'fish' sense survives only in compounds (물고기 'live fish'). For fish-as-food modern Korean uses 생선 not bare 고기. Listing 'fish' as a coequal gloss misleads learners. Wiktionary corroborates the meat-primary, fish-archaic split.

entries.gloss: to do for the sake of

auditFix.issue: 식 standalone does not mean 'meal'. The 'meal' sense only appears in compounds like 식사, 한식, 양식. Bare 식 means 'ceremony', 'formula' (math), or 'expression/style'. Listing 'meal' as a standalone gloss is misleading for learners.
아 is an interjection (exclamation). PoS should be 'interjection', not 'noun/adv'. (As a vocative particle 아 is a particle, also not a noun/adv.)
온통 is an adverb ('all over, entirely, throughout', as in 온통 빨갛다). PoS should be 'adverb'.

이리 in modern Korean is an adverb ('this way, hither, like this'), not a noun. The 'noun' option in 'noun/adv' is wrong. (Historically 이리 also meant 'wolf' but that sense is now obsolete in favor of 늑대.)
이미 is unambiguously an adverb ('already'). It is never used as a noun. PoS should be 'adverb'.

Confirmed: 장 is one of the most polysemous Sino-Korean syllables (chapter 章, market 場, sheet-counter 張, intestines 腸, head/chief 長, sauce 醬, etc.). The PoS 'noun/adv' is wrong for the counter sense (counters are not adverbs). At minimum, top three senses + correct PoS should be captured.

entries.gloss: not at all, (not) in the least

auditFix.issue: 전혀 is an adverb ('not at all, never', requires negative predicate). PoS 'noun/adv' is incorrect — it is never used as a noun.

Standalone 한 is the native-Korean numeral determiner 'one' (한 사람 = one person), or a prefix/intensifier ('한가운데' = the very middle). It does not mean 'Korean' on its own; the 'Korean' sense only emerges in Sino-Korean compounds like 한국, 한복, 한식. PoS should be 'determiner' rather than 'noun/adv'.

entries.gloss: thing, fact (bound noun, colloquial form of 것)

auditFix.issue: Confirmed: 거 is the colloquial contraction of 것, classified as a bound noun (의존명사) — it cannot stand alone, and combines as 게 (것이), 걸 (것을), 건 (것은). Tagging as 'noun/adv' is incorrect (not an adverb) and obscures bound status. Wiktionary corroborates.

고프다 is a bound adjective that essentially only collocates with 배 (배(가) 고프다 = 'to be hungry', literally 'stomach is empty/hungry'). It cannot freely mean 'hungry' attached to a person; *나는 고파요 is awkward. Without the 배 collocation note, learners produce ungrammatical sentences.

Confirmed: 년 (年) is a bound counter for years (2024년, 삼 년) requiring Sino-Korean numerals — the free standalone noun for 'year' is 해. Tagging as 'noun/adv' obscures counter status and the obligatory numeric host. Wiktionary classifies as Sino-Korean counter/bound noun.
대단히 (the -히 form) is unambiguously an adverb ('very, extremely, greatly'). It is never a noun. PoS should be 'adverb'.

Both senses are real (plural particle -들 and noun 들 'field/plain'), but they are different parts of speech: the plural marker is a particle/suffix, while 들 'field' is a noun. PoS 'noun/adv' covers neither cleanly. 들 is also never an adverb.
딱 is an adverb meaning 'exactly, precisely, just right' (딱 맞다, 딱 한 번). It is also a mimetic for snapping/cracking sounds. It is not a noun. The 'noun' element of 'noun/adv' is wrong.

맨 is primarily a prefix meaning 'bare/naked, nothing but' (맨손 'bare hand', 맨발 'bare foot', 맨바닥 'bare ground'). Only as a determiner before nouns of position/order does it intensify to 'the very (most)' (맨 앞, 맨 처음). The current gloss captures only the secondary sense and omits the dominant 'bare' meaning.

Confirmed: 북 'drum' (native Korean word) is fully standalone, while 북 'north' (北) is mostly bound — natural everyday usage is 북쪽/북부, not bare 북. Listing 'north' first as coequal misleads learners. Reordering is a defensible fix.
없이 is an adverb ('without'), derived from 없다 + -이. It is never a noun.

The gloss correctly identifies 여 as a prefix (Sino-Korean 女, used in 여학생, 여배우, 여왕). However the partOfSpeech 'noun/adv' contradicts the gloss; it should be 'prefix'. 여 does not function as a standalone noun or adverb.
오랫동안 functions adverbially ('for a long time'). It is morphologically a noun phrase (오랜 + 동안) but is not used as a standalone noun in modern usage; it occupies an adverbial slot.
완전히 (the -히 form) is unambiguously an adverb. PoS should be 'adverb'. (The noun is 완전.)

Confirmed: 이렇다 is the dictionary form of an adjective meaning 'to be like this; to be such'. The gloss 'like this' reads as the adverbial form 이렇게. For the headword, 'to be like this' is the accurate gloss. (How to Study Korean and Wiktionary corroborate.)
인분 is a counter (Sino-Korean 人分) for food portions (이 인분 = two servings). PoS 'noun/adv' is incorrect; it should be 'counter'. The gloss already correctly identifies it as a counter.

Confirmed: 적 has at least three unrelated lexemes — 적 (敵) 'enemy', 적 (occasion/time, e.g., 어렸을 적에), and the productive Sino-Korean suffix -적 (的) 'pertaining to' (사회적, 과학적). The current gloss omits the highly productive suffix sense, which is among the most important to a Korean learner. Wiktionary documents all three.

Confirmed: 정말 is most often used as an adverb 'really, truly' (etymologically 正 'true' + 말 'word'), and is also a noun meaning 'the truth, real fact'. The PoS tag should lead with adverb since the gloss 'really' is the adverbial sense.

제법 in this sense ('quite, considerably, fairly') is an adverb (제법 잘하다, 제법 춥다). The homograph noun 제법 (製法) 'method of manufacture' is unrelated and not the gloss given. PoS 'noun/adv' is misleading for the gloss 'quite, fairly'.
주로 is unambiguously an adverb meaning 'mainly, mostly, primarily'. PoS should be 'adverb', not 'noun/adv'. The homograph 주로 (走路) 'racetrack' is a different lexeme not represented by this gloss.
함께 is unambiguously an adverb. PoS should be 'adverb'.
가만히 (-히 form) is an adverb ('quietly, still, motionlessly'). It is never a noun. PoS should be 'adverb'.

같이 functions as an adverb ('together', e.g., 같이 먹다) and as a postpositional particle attached to nouns ('like, as', e.g., 달같이 밝다). It is never a noun. The 'noun' element of 'noun/adv' is incorrect; PoS should be 'adverb' (or 'adverb/particle' to capture both senses cleanly). Mirrors the audited fix for 함께 (idx 491).

entries.gloss: moreover, in addition, on top of that

auditFix.issue: 게다가 is a conjunctive adverb ('moreover, in addition, on top of that'). It is never a noun. PoS should be 'adverb' or 'conjunction'.

entries.gloss: as it is, just like that, intact

auditFix.issue: 그대로 is an adverb ('as it is, just like that, intact'). It can also occupy noun-phrase slots loosely, but is not classified as a noun. PoS should be 'adverb'.

Confirmed: 그만 is primarily an adverb ('that much; no more, enough; involuntarily'), not a verb 'stop'. Wiktionary and language-learning sources all classify it as an adverb/interjection. The verb form is 그만하다/그만두다. Current 'noun/adv' tag is wrong (no noun sense) and the gloss 'stop' invites grammatical errors.

기본 is a noun meaning 'foundation, basis, fundamentals' (Sino-Korean 基本). 'basic' is an adjective in English, but 기본 itself is a noun (the adjective form is 기본적 or 기본의/기본적인). Glossing as 'basic' invites the learner to use 기본 as an adjective, which is wrong.

The parenthetical '(counter)' is misleading. 네 is not itself a counter — it is the modifier/determiner form of the native Korean numeral 넷 ('four'), used immediately before counters (네 사람 'four people', 네 권 'four books'). A learner reading 'four (counter)' could mistakenly assume 네 functions as a counting word like 명/권/장. Better gloss: 'yes; four (before counters)' or 'yes; four (modifier form of 넷)'.

senses: four (before counters, modifier form of 넷)

entries.gloss: right in front of one's eyes

auditFix.issue: 똑같이 is an adverb meaning 'identically / in the same way / equally', describing how an action is done. The English gloss 'exactly the same' reads as an adjectival phrase modifying a noun. A learner seeing this gloss could mis-use it as an adjective. Better gloss: 'identically; in the same way; equally'.

않다 is an auxiliary/negation verb almost exclusively used in the construction V-지 않다 ('does not V' / 'is not Adj'). It inherits verb-or-adjective behavior from the predicate it negates rather than meaning 'to do not' on its own. The bare gloss 'not to do' suggests an active independent verb meaning 'refrain from doing', which obscures its grammaticalised auxiliary role. A learner gloss should signal the auxiliary nature, e.g. '(auxiliary) to not do/be (with -지)'.

Confirmed: 연기 has three common Sino-Korean homonyms — 煙氣 'smoke', 演技 'performance/acting', 延期 'postponement'. The third sense (postponement) is genuinely common in everyday Korean (회의를 연기하다 'postpone the meeting'). Wiktionary documents all three; the existing two-sense gloss is incomplete.

전자 is a noun with two main senses: 電子 'electron' (the physics particle) and 前者 'the former' (in comparisons, opposite of 후자 'the latter'). The current gloss 'electronic' is an English adjective and only loosely covers usage in compounds like 전자제품. Standalone 전자 is not adjectival. Better: 'electron; the former'.
